engine.meaning: Nearly the original verbatim, so every fact, date and number survives, but "50% of proceeds dead set on long-term on-chain liquidity support" makes the commitment of funds read as a determination.
engine.sense: Of its four changes, two take the wrong sense: "dead set on" means determined to, not 'dedicated to', in both "50% of proceeds dead set on long-term on-chain liquidity support" and "**50% of proceeds were dead set on long-term on-chain liquidity support.**". "Nah, nah." and "Yep." fit.
engine.authenticity: The few Aussie touches sit on untouched formal prose: "Nah, nah. The auction determined allocations and a clearing price within the auction itself."
engine.register: Essentially untranslated: four small changes in the whole FAQ, far below level 3.
engine.tone: The original's plain FAQ tone is intact, as the text is, apart from the slightly flip "Nah, nah." on a price question.
engine.flow: Reads as the original does; "dead set on long-term on-chain liquidity support" jars.
engine.essence: Unmistakably the original FAQ, being nearly the original.

yarn-deadset.meaning: Every fact, date and number survives: "**50% of proceeds were set aside for long-term on-chain liquidity support.**", "The minimum price for each following period is the higher of the original floor price or the clearing price of the period before." Legal notices kept intact.
yarn-deadset.sense: Fits throughout: "Bids that get up within a period", "take the sting out of sniping", "The first auction is done and dusted", "still up for grabs in the final period", "spread FOLD round more widely".
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural Aussie English in a docs voice: "It's for people who had a go in the auction", "Nah, nah.", "links sent to you out of the blue in DMs".
yarn-deadset.register: Level 3: the FAQ in a relaxed Aussie voice without asides; legal notices left formal, as they should be. No swearing.
yarn-deadset.tone: Keeps the clear, careful FAQ tone and firm safety warnings: "Interfold team members and moderators will never ask for your seed phrase".
yarn-deadset.flow: Smooth, with a repeated preposition: "They got through the required verification process through the official flow." and "get through identity verification through the official verification process".
yarn-deadset.variety: Varied: "had a go", "four lots", "kicked off", "done and dusted", "get up", "up for grabs", "take the sting out of", "switched on".
yarn-deadset.essence: Unmistakably the FOLD Auction FAQ, structure, tables, code and links intact.

yarn-troppo.meaning: All facts survive, but it adds claims and judgments: "that was on purpose, not stinginess", "so it's anyone's game right to the end", "cutting it fine", "Anyone who reckons they know is having a lend of ya."
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "Bids that get up", "take the wind out of the snipers who'd jump in at the last second", "into more people's mitts", "If it smells shonky, it probably is."
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Plenty of real idiom ("having a lend of ya", "shonky", "done and dusted"), with stock yarn lines bolted on: "Here's one for ya.", "pull up a stool, this one's for you".
yarn-troppo.register: Far heavier than level 3: a pub-yarn frame and a tag on nearly every paragraph ("Righto.", "Here's the clever bit.", "Job done.", "That's the lawyers' bit."). No swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: A careful token-sale FAQ becomes a chummy pitch: "keeping yourself safe from the sharks", "Think of Auction 2 as a little warm-up lap", "That's the lawyers' bit." The safety warnings stay firm.
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads aloud easily, but the asides pile up: "It's all still there waiting for ya.", "so don't go looking for the button."
yarn-troppo.variety: Very varied: "had a crack", "mitts", "warm-up lap", "leg-up", "up for grabs", "lend of ya", "rock up", "shonky", "nitty-gritty".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the FAQ, but its shape as a sober reference document is turned into a yarn: "This FAQ is the full yarn on FOLD Auction 2".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Complete and accurate: "**50% of proceeds were locked in for long-term on-chain liquidity support.**", "Getting through verification didn't guarantee you eligibility or an allocation, mind.", legal notices intact.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Exact: "locked in" for committed, "Bids that get up", "take the wind out of sniping", "find their own level", "links that turn up out of the blue in DMs".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural throughout: "It's for anyone who got in on the auction", "That one's all done and dusted", "get FOLD into more hands", "mind".
yarn-dinkum.register: Level 3: a clear Aussie voice with no asides; legal notices kept formal. No swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the careful FAQ tone and firm warnings: "will never ask for your seed phrase, private key, wallet backup, or access to your wallet. Not ever."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "The CCA hands tokens out bit by bit, at the one price within each period."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Good range ("got in on", "off the ground", "leg-up", "done and dusted", "up for grabs", "find their own level"), with "switch on"/"switched on" recurring.

unharnessed.meaning: Nearly everything survives, but "stop sniping" overstates the original's 'mitigate sniping', and "what FOLD's actually worth or what it'll trade at" slightly expands the risk notice.

unharnessed.variety: Reasonable range ("had a go", "four lots", "done and dusted", "up for grabs", "gas wars", "down the track", "dodgy").
